verifications.note: FGT/Panhandle Energy's own Phase VIII project-description page (NRC-archived ADAMS copy): 'The project will provide an annual average of 820,000 MMbtu/day of additional firm transportation capacity' — names Phase VIII directly.

Southern Union Co. 2010 10-K, Florida Gas Transmission Phase VIII discussion: 'approximately 820 MMcf/d' of expansion capacity, with 'firm transportation service agreements with shippers ... accounting for approximately 74 percent of the available expansion capacity'.

EIA Today in Energy, on FGT: 'placed its Phase VIII Expansion project in service on April 1, 2011' and the expansion 'increased FGT's design capacity by 0.82 billion cubic feet per day' — 0.82 Bcf/d = 820 MMcf/d, an exact match to the recorded 820.00 MMcf/d.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Three independent sources (FGT/Panhandle's own project page as archived by NRC, Southern Union's SEC 10-K, and EIA) all give 820 MMcf/d (or its 820,000 MMBtu/d / 0.82 Bcf/d equivalent) for the Phase VIII Expansion, matching the recorded Capacity=820.00 MMcf/d exactly.

verifications.note: FERC pre-filing scoping notice for Phase VIII lists each segment's diameter by name: Loop 1 '42-inch-diameter pipeline'; Loops 2-10 '36-inch-diameter pipeline'; Loop 11 (Turkey Point Lateral) '24-inch-diameter pipeline'; Arcadia to FPL Martin Plant Lateral '30-inch-diameter pipeline'; Manatee Lateral '24-inch-diameter pipeline' — covers all four recorded diameters (24, 30, 36, 42 in).

Industrial Info Resources, on FGT Phase VIII: 'approximately 400 miles of 36" and 30" diameter pipeline looping' plus '100 miles of new 36" diameter pipeline' — independently corroborates the 30-in and 36-in diameters.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The May 2008 FERC pre-filing scoping notice (E8-11695) is the only source found that breaks out every individual loop/lateral diameter for Phase VIII, and it names all four recorded values (24, 30, 36, 42 in); Industrial Info Resources independently corroborates 30 and 36 in. Flagging one discrepancy: that same scoping notice also lists two smaller segments at 20-inch diameter (the ~22-mi Suwannee Lateral and the ~22.7-mi acquired FPL Martin-to-mainline pipeline) that do not appear in the sheet's recorded diameter set. The scoping notice's total project estimate (567.6 mi) shrank to 483.2 mi by the time FGT filed its formal certificate application in Oct. 2008 (per FR-2008-11-21/E8-27688, matching the sheet's recorded 483.00 mi Length), so the 20-in segments most likely fell out of the certificated, as-built scope — recorded Diameter looks correct, but this is inferred from the mileage drop rather than a document that states the final diameter list directly; tier set to medium rather than high on that basis.

verifications.note: FGT/Panhandle Phase VIII project page: 'Florida Gas Transmission is proposing to expand its natural gas pipeline system' and 'Natural gas is the primary fuel for new electric generation plants'.
FERC scoping notice: FGT's 'proposed Phase VIII Expansion Project' involves 'construction and operation of natural gas pipeline and compressor facilities'.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources describe the Phase VIII facilities explicitly as natural gas pipeline, confirming recorded Fuel=Gas.

verifications.note: 'The Phase VIII Expansion Project will consist of approximately 483.2 miles of multi diameter pipeline in Alabama, Mississippi and Florida' — 0.2 mi over the recorded 483.00 mi, within rounding.

FERC certificate application notice (Docket CP09-17-000), Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC: FGT proposes to '(i) Construct and operate 483.2 miles of pipeline loop, mainline, and laterals' — same figure, independent filing.
EIA: FGT 'placed its Phase VIII Expansion project in service on April 1, 2011', a project that included '483.2 miles of new pipeline'.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Three independent sources (FGT/Panhandle's own page, FERC's certificate-application Federal Register notice, and EIA) all give 483.2 mi, agreeing within rounding with the recorded 483.00 mi. Note the project's earlier May-2008 pre-filing estimate (federalregister E8-11695, already open on this row for other columns) put the total at 567.6 mi before the certificated scope was finalized at 483.2 mi in the Oct-2008 application — the recorded value matches the final, as-built figure, not the initial estimate.

verifications.note: 'Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC's (FGT) proposed Phase VIII Expansion Project' — FGT is named as the entity that would 'construct, operate, and maintain the proposed facilities', i.e. the owning/operating entity of this segment.

PHMSA special-permit request: 'Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (FGT) requests a special permit' for segments of its own pipeline system, and lists 'Southeast Division — Florida Gas Transmission' as the operating division — confirms FGT LLC as the current owner/operator of the pipeline system this segment belongs to.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Recorded Owner1 = 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' at 100% is the operating-company entity itself, matching both sources' identification of FGT LLC as the party that builds, owns, and operates its own pipeline system (as distinct from FGT's corporate parent Citrus Corp., which a 2011 Energy Transfer release describes as the 50/50 El Paso/Southern Union joint venture that in turn owns 100% of FGT LLC — that parent-level ownership is not what the sheet's Owner column records here).

verifications.note: 'FGT estimates the total cost of the project will be $2,455 million' — exact match to the recorded 2,455,000,000.00 USD.
FERC certificate application notice: 'FGT estimates that the proposed facilities will cost approximately $2.455 billion' — same exact figure, independent filing.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Two independent sources (FGT/Panhandle's own project page and the FERC Federal Register certificate-application notice) both give $2,455 million / $2.455 billion, an exact match to the recorded SegmentCost. (The Southern Union 2010 10-K, already open on this row, gives a slightly different final-accounting figure of 'approximately $2.48 billion, including capitalized equity and debt costs', with 'approximately $2.2 billion' recorded as of year-end 2010 — noted here as a nearby but distinct figure, not used as one of the two refs above since it reflects final capitalized cost rather than the original $2.455bn estimate the sheet records.)

verifications.note: 'The project is expected to be completed and in service in the spring of 2011', and the page's posted-filings list shows 'April 1, 2011 - Phase VIII In Service Notification (pdf)'.
Southern Union 10-K on Phase VIII: In-Service Date 'April 2011'.
EIA: FGT 'placed its Phase VIII Expansion project in service on April 1, 2011'.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Three independent sources agree the Phase VIII segment entered service April 2011, matching recorded StartYear1=2011.

verifications.note: EIA discusses FGT flows in the period after Phase VIII's April 2011 in-service date, noting 'daily natural gas flows into Florida have exceeded the pre-expanded capacity nearly 50% of the time' since then — describing an operating, flowing pipeline, not a shelved/idle one.

2021 PHMSA special-permit request from FGT for segments of its own operating pipeline system, including 'relevant operating information including operating pressure, leak history' for the segments in question — filed a decade after Phase VIII's in-service date, evidence the FGT mainline (of which Phase VIII is part) remains an actively operated system, with no indication of retirement/abandonment anywhere found.

resolutions.researcher_notes: No source found states 'Phase VIII is currently operating' in so many words (as expected for a decade-old, routine expansion increment); status is corroborated indirectly via (a) EIA's description of ongoing post-2011 flows through the expanded system and (b) a 2021 PHMSA filing showing FGT still actively operating and reporting on its pipeline segments a decade later, with no retirement, abandonment, or replacement of the Phase VIII facilities found in any source consulted (federalregister, SEC, NRC, EIA, PHMSA, industrialinfo, naturalgasintel). Tier set to medium given the indirect nature of the confirmation.
